# 2 Kings 20 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 2 Kings 20 (21 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Total disagreements logged:** 5

---

## V.1 — "Command your house" vs. "Set your house in order" vs. "Put your affairs in order"
- **EMET:** "Command your house" / **LOGOS:** "Set your house in order" / **PNEUMA:** "Put your affairs in order"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Set your house in order" — traditional English idiom that captures *tsav le-veytekha*.

---

## V.3 — "in truth" vs. "in faithfulness" vs. "faithfully"
- **EMET:** "in truth" / **LOGOS:** "in faithfulness" / **PNEUMA:** "faithfully"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "in faithfulness" — captures the covenantal dimension of *emet*.

---

## V.7 — "cake of figs" vs. "paste of figs"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "cake of figs" / **PNEUMA:** "paste of figs"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "cake of figs" — *develah* is a pressed fig cake, not a paste.

---

## V.13 — "listened" vs. "welcomed" vs. "was delighted"
- **EMET:** "listened to them" / **LOGOS:** "welcomed them" / **PNEUMA:** "was delighted by the attention"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "welcomed them" — *shama'* here means to receive favorably; PNEUMA adds psychological interpretation not in the Hebrew.

---

## V.19 — Hezekiah's response: ambiguous vs. selfish
- **EMET:** question form (ambiguous) / **LOGOS:** "For he thought..." (preserves ambiguity) / **PNEUMA:** "At least there will be peace..." (resolved as selfish)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** Preserves ambiguity with "For he thought, 'Is it not so...'" — allows both readings.

---
*— SOPHIA*
